This is a busy month for us, and I need you to help me out with a few different things.

Firstly, can you please write a script for a short publicity video to introduce the AIBookPioneer? I think we need to cover basic information on what it is, what the user experiences and address any concerns people might have.
Secondly, Mr Chan needs a preliminary report on this awful moth infestation. Write a brief summary of how this happened, what we know about the moth situation now and make some recommendations.

Finally, I’ve decided to submit the People Library idea for the LCSD Community Ties Project. Could you write a proposal? Include: what a People Library is and how it works; how the People Library started; and the positive impacts it potentially has. Start by looking at the Leisure and Cultural Services Department notice and the Tom Yengi interview. Plus, take a look at the data from the Tokyo event and see if you can make some generalisations from it to include.
Thanks for the help – you’re doing a great job as our new intern!
Leisure and Cultural Services Department (LCSD) notice

Every year, the LCSD invites Hong Kong libraries to submit their proposals for the LCSD Community Ties Project. The winning entry will be chosen based on which proposed project can best contribute to improving community ties and have the biggest positive impact in Hong Kong in the coming year.
The winning idea will be fully funded by the LCSD.
by Katy Milanovic (Assistant Librarian, Adelaide Library)

For those of you who haven’t ever experienced a People Library…think of a hall full of really interesting storytellers. Each on their own little platform, telling the story of their daily lives. I can still remember the first People Library event I went to in 2018. The storytellers were all street cleaners here in Adelaide. I loved how we could ask questions – I learnt so much. That’s the great thing about People Library events – you can ask questions and really engage with the speakers.
So, I was excited when I heard that Tom Yengi, one of the founders of the People Library, was visiting our library here in Adelaide this week. We made some time to have a chat.

So, Tom, we have many regulars at our People Library events here in Adelaide every month and we know they’ll be interested to hear from you. So how did you first get the idea to do a People Library event?
Well, I don’t know if you remember but a lot of refugees arrived in Australia in the early 2000s. Some people weren’t very welcoming towards them…
I was a bit young to really remember, but I’ve read about it.
Right. Well, I wanted to see if I could tackle people’s prejudices by giving them the chance to hear more about the refugees’ lives.
So that was your main motivation?
Yeah. You know, prejudice can easily arise when groups of people don’t know much about each other.
Yeah, so a couple of us planned an event at our library in Darwin, where people could come along and hear more from the refugees themselves. That was in 2002.
Well, it’s certainly something that you yourself must be immensely proud of. And what about you nowadays? What do you do now?
Well, I’ve just been appointed to be the librarian on the Pitcairn Islands in the Pacific Ocean. It’s the most remote library in the world.
Sounds like a big adventure! Well, thanks so much for coming in today, Tom. It’s been lovely to talk to you.
Go on to the next page
Anyone able to help? We’ve just discovered moths in our library. Any suggestions?
We had bedbugs last year. Count yourself lucky.
Moths destroyed our carpet last year. You definitely need to get some professionals in to advise.
Yeah, we’re starting to realise that. We thought we could just vacuum them away…

Hey, sorry to hear this. I’m at a small branch and we’ve somehow managed to have two infestations in 3 years – bedbugs and cockroaches! One thing we did which has proved helpful is we got someone in to give a talk to staff on common pests. Everyone kind of knows what signs to look out for now.
Yes, we did the same thing. Two months ago, one of our librarians managed to spot some cockroaches moving in before the situation got out of hand.
@Librarian123. Did you have to close the library while dealing with everything?
Oh, you’ll definitely need to close. You’ll need professionals in to do a deep clean and you can’t have people around while they’re working.
We had a cockroach infestation once and we had to do a freeze treatment on all our books. I strongly recommend you do this, or you’ll have the same problem again in a few months.
No, it depends on what insect it is. It’s not always necessary. You only need to do it if it’s cockroaches, not moths.
Email to registered participants: Bangkok People Library event
Subject: The People Library Bangkok Follow-up
Thank you for attending our first ever People Library event here in Bangkok last week. We wanted to let you know what one of our storytellers had to say afterwards:

I’ve been homeless and living on the streets for so long that I got used to being invisible, to people not even seeing me. So I was so nervous when I was asked to stand up and talk about myself. Who would be interested in me? But since I did it, I feel that I want to contribute. That’s what I was explaining to my counsellor yesterday. I have even started volunteering, serving food at the homeless centre – Isra.
Thanks again for your support. We’ll see you again next month when we will be hearing stories from migrant workers living in Bangkok.
Email thread: Teckniti Consultants and Thomas Chan
Subject: Re: Re: Re: Victoria Harbour Library and book explorer options

AIBookPioneer has the upper hand in that regard due to the fact that they are using a new bespoke technology called DickensTech. When I myself tried it out, I found it remarkably seamless and definitely superior to NarrativeTravel, despite my initial reservations.
Thanks for getting back to me so promptly. Is there any difference in the quality of the tools in terms of them malfunctioning?

I’d say from the outset that both AIBookPioneer and NarrativeTravel offer historically and geographically accurate 3D worlds and are both as visually powerful as each other. So there isn’t too much to choose between them. Both offer around 500 books. AIBookPioneer also includes books written in Korean. NarrativeTravel offers more variety, with books in 7 languages.

Users of NarrativeTravel are actually standing up so they can move around in the scene. I personally think the ability to physically move creates a better all-round experience. Users of AIBookPioneer, on the other hand, are required to stay in their seats inside the AIBookPioneer for the duration. So if you’re pressed for space, this will be the more appropriate option.
Let me know if there is anything else.
Thanks for meeting with me last week to discuss the choice of a “book explorer” tool for our new FutureAI Centre. We still haven’t decided between AIBookPioneer and NarrativeTravel.
I understand both provide access to books written in Chinese and English – does either offer literature in other languages? Which has the widest variety of books to choose from?

As our library is in Hong Kong, space, of course, is at an absolute premium. You said that one of the tools allows users to walk around in the recreated scene from the book. Which one was that? I really don’t think we have the space for that in the room we’ve allocated to the FutureAI Centre.

What on earth is going on? I was studying this evening, and I saw THREE horrible little moths on the floor! I am NOT okay with this.
I saw one too. I just moved to a different section. No need to overreact.
This morning there was a whole family of them on the carpet. I couldn’t concentrate. They’re so gross. I’m not studying here again, that’s for sure.
They’re definitely taking over. One ran on my hand! Does no one at the library check these comments?? Now I’ll have to use my school library. It’s so noisy. Aaah!
LOL, this is hilarious. Maybe we should make a short video about the moths taking over the library.
Don’t be childish. If the situation is really that bad, why don’t you talk to the librarians instead of just whining here?
I did! I couldn’t even read the newspaper in peace this evening, so I told one of the librarians about it. She didn’t do anything – just laughed!!!
Was she wearing an intern badge? They’re usually on duty in the evenings. They spend most of their time on Instagram…
I’ve posted the video about the moths. Check it out! Here’s the link:

Transcript of telephone call between Powerful Pest Controllers and Agnes Yip
Powerful Pest Controllers, how may we help you?
Hi Ben, it’s Agnes from Victoria Harbour Library. You were over here on Sunday checking out our moth situation?
Oh yes, that’s right. We’re working on your report now.
Right… Well, it’s just that our chief librarian is really stressed out about the whole situation and wants an update as soon as possible. What can you tell me at this point?
Well… we need time to check the specimens we took and consider the best way forward.
Yes, I do understand that… but I’m under pressure here.

Well, they’ve done a bit of damage to your carpet in the far corner of the Adults Section. You’ll probably have to get that whole section of carpet pulled up and put a new one in. Just to be on the safe side.
You mean all of the carpet in the Adults Section?
Oh okay. Can’t we just give it a vacuum?
A vacuum? No, you’re going to need to get some professionals in for a proper clean.
The entire library? Oh, Thomas is not going to be happy about that. For how long?
At least 48 hours I reckon. We can confirm everything in the report but for now, this is what I expect.
Okay then, well, have a good weekend.
So, after the meeting this morning, I was reading about these “book explorer” tools and apparently lots of people have complained about them glitching. They have a pretty bad reputation.

Yep, but Thomas told me that the guy at Teckniti Consultants said that AIBookPioneer uses this amazing technology they designed themselves. So all that’s a thing of the past. The technology has a cool name but I can’t remember it right now.
Definitely mention it by name in the video then. You asked me to look into why no-one was checking the comments on our pages?
You mean the stuff about the moths?
Exactly…I checked and those interns we had last month were supposed to be keeping an eye on the comments.
Those interns were terrible! They never did anything!!!
Well, I looked at the Completed Duties Log and they definitely hadn’t done the social media stuff.
As I said, those interns weren’t the best.
On another note, I was thinking a bit about your proposal for the community ties project.
Yeah, I remembered that I received a really lovely email from the Bangkok People Library organiser. I’ll forward it to you. There might be stuff you can include in your proposal.
Ok, great. Yes, forward it to me.
